title: What If the Sky Went Dark for 18 Months? Europe Lived It

scenes.text: What if the sun dimmed for eighteen months? In the year 536, it did.
A volcano in Iceland threw ash across the Northern Hemisphere, and a haze dimmed the sky from Europe to Asia.
Summer temperatures fell by roughly one and a half to two and a half degrees Celsius, starting the coldest decade in 2,300 years.
Snow reportedly fell in a Chinese summer. Crops failed, and people starved.
Then in 542 a plague struck the Eastern Roman Empire and killed millions.
The proof sits in Swiss glacier ice: tiny glass shards from Icelandic rock. One eruption changed the world.
